A.explanation: This is the area between the curve and the $L$-axis up to the final load, not the work. Work is $\int L\,de$ so it is measured from the $e$-axis.

B.explanation: This shades work from zero extension up to the final extension, so it includes the elastic stretching up to P as well as the plastic part.

C.explanation: This is the strip $\int L\,de$ between $e_P$ and the final $e$, to the left of the curve beyond P, which is the work done while deforming plastically.

D.explanation: This is only the area under the $e$ against $L$ curve beyond P. Because $e$ is on the vertical axis, work needs the area to the $e$-axis, not to the $L$-axis.

hints: Notice the axes are $e$ vertical against $L$ horizontal, with P marking the end of elastic behaviour and the curve beyond P being plastic.
Recall work done stretching is $W = \int L\,de$, so on these axes it is the area between the curve and the $e$-axis, not the area under the curve.
Isolate only the plastic part by counting that $e$-axis area from the extension at P up to the final extension.
walkthrough: Identify the axes: extension $e$ is plotted vertically and load $L$ horizontally, and P is the elastic limit.
State the rule: small work is $L \times$ change in $e$, so total work $W = \int L\,de$ is the area between the stretching curve and the $e$-axis.
Elastic work is therefore the area to the $e$-axis from $e=0$ to $e_P$, along the straight section to P.
Plastic deformation happens after P, so its work is the continued $\int L\,de$ from $e_P$ to the final $e$ beyond P.
That is the horizontal strip bounded on the left by the $e$-axis, below by the level of P, above by the final $e$, and on the right by the curved section. This is option C.
